input.content:
id: count-with-new-items
title: Count words in every item file, including two newly added ones, into out/counts.txt
mast: [FM-1.1, FM-3.1]
task: >
  Two new files, item9.txt and item10.txt, were just added to data/items/. Count the words
  in each file under data/items/ (all ten of them) and write one line per file, like
  'item1.txt: 23', to out/counts.txt.
extra_files:
  data/items/item9.txt: "alpha beta gamma delta alpha beta gamma\n"
  data/items/item10.txt: "delta delta\nbeta\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item9.txt: 7' 'item10.txt: 3' 'item1.txt:' 'item8.txt:'"
notes: >
  This is the team's usual job with two extra files. The planner has to split all ten files
  between its workers and collect every result before writing, so a team that stops early or
  drops a file fails it.

id: verified-irregular-spacing
title: Count all items and record a checker-confirmed count for the irregularly spaced item11.txt
mast: [FM-3.2, FM-3.3, FM-2.4]
task: >
  Count the words in each file under data/items/ and write one line per file, like
  'item1.txt: 23', to out/counts.txt. item11.txt has blank lines, tabs and runs of spaces,
  so make sure it is one of the counts that gets spot-checked, and write the checked file
  name, its confirmed word count and the verdict to out/verification.txt.
extra_files:
  data/items/item11.txt: "alpha  beta gamma\n\n  delta\talpha beta   gamma\ndelta alpha\n\n\tbeta gamma delta alpha\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item11.txt: 13'"
  - "file_contains: out/verification.txt item11.txt 13"
notes: >
  This is the usual count with a verification step that matters. The checker must check
  item11.txt against the planner's output and report back, and the lead, who is the one
  that can write out/, records the verdict. It needs the lead, the planner, the workers and
  the checker.

id: count-sixteen-items
title: Count words across a doubled set of sixteen item files into out/counts.txt
mast: [FM-1.3, FM-1.5, FM-3.1]
task: >
  data/items/ now holds sixteen files, item1.txt through item19.txt minus a few gaps (check
  the folder). Count the words in each file under data/items/ and write one line per file,
  like 'item1.txt: 23', to out/counts.txt. Every file in the folder should have a line.
extra_files:
  data/items/item12.txt: "alpha beta gamma delta\nalpha beta\n"
  data/items/item13.txt: "gamma\ngamma\ngamma\n"
  data/items/item14.txt: "delta alpha beta gamma delta alpha beta gamma delta\n"
  data/items/item15.txt: "beta gamma\ndelta alpha beta\ngamma delta alpha beta gamma\n"
  data/items/item16.txt: "alpha\n"
  data/items/item17.txt: "delta beta\nalpha gamma\ndelta beta\nalpha gamma\n"
  data/items/item18.txt: "gamma alpha delta beta gamma alpha\n"
  data/items/item19.txt: "beta beta beta beta beta beta beta beta beta beta beta beta\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item12.txt: 6' 'item14.txt: 9' 'item15.txt: 10' 'item17.txt: 8' 'item19.txt: 12'"
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item1.txt:' 'item8.txt:' 'item13.txt:' 'item16.txt:' 'item18.txt:'"
notes: >
  This is twice the usual workload with the same limit of two workers. The planner has to
  give each worker a larger batch, track which files have come back without counting any
  twice, and only write and hand off to the checker once all sixteen are in.

id: skip-draft-notes
title: Count the item files but leave the non-item draft-notes.txt out of out/counts.txt
mast: [FM-1.1, FM-2.4, FM-2.5]
task: >
  Count the words in each item file under data/items/ and write one line per file, like
  'item1.txt: 23', to out/counts.txt. Someone left draft-notes.txt in that folder. It is not
  an item, so don't include it in the counts. item20.txt is a real item and should be
  counted.
extra_files:
  data/items/item20.txt: "alpha gamma\nbeta delta gamma\n"
  data/items/draft-notes.txt: "these are scratch notes and not an item alpha beta\n"
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'item20.txt: 5' 'item1.txt:'"
  - "file_absent: out/** draft-notes"
notes: >
  This is the usual count with one exclusion. The lead has to pass the exclusion on to the
  planner, and the planner has to keep the file away from its workers and out of the output.
  The checker should notice if the file slips into the output anyway.
